newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Central Bank for privatising state banks.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Central Bank for privatising state banks.

text.p: Sri Lanka's two state banks, the Bank of Ceylon and the People's Bank, need to be privatised to improve their operational efficiency, the Central Bank said in its annual report released on Wednesday.
Alternatively, the two state banks can be restructured, within state ownership, to improve their commercial viability, said the report, a copy which was obtained by Reuters.

"This is essential, particularly in the context of increasing competition in the financial system where the two state banks have to compete not only with their counterparts but also with other non-commercial banks," the report said.
The two state banks still account for nearly two-thirds of the total assets of the banking system and any inefficiencies are quickly transmitted to the entire financial system, it said.
"Privatisation of state banks is a delicate issue and may not be immediately feasible as a great deal of preparatory work would have to be undertaken," said the report.
"...it is essential that the public and the employees be made aware of potential benefits of privatisation," it said.
